business_problem: BEEST just won the 2026 KeHE Golden Ticket - nationwide distribution is arriving before consumer awareness. With ~2 employees and DTC/independent-only sales, the crunch-verified product has no trial engine at retail: shoppers cannot know it is crunchy until they bite it, and nothing on shelf says 'this is not the jerky you hate.'

objectives.text: Drive 1,200 attributed purchases (retail code + online code) in 45 days and lift trial-to-repeat among sampled shoppers
Run 1,600 blind crunch-test samples and generate 4,000 coupon claims
Reach 800K Texas impressions and get 'crunch verified' remembered by surveyed shoppers

findings.finding: Content analysis of 38 public site reviews (collected 2026-11-07): 42% mention taste/flavor, 21% texture/crunch, 18% compare it directly to jerky/meat snacks, avg rating 4.34/5 with real complaints present
findings.therefore: The crunch is the story - demos and blind crunch tests lead; the review corpus is small but honest enough to show both love and friction

findings.finding: Verbatim review: 'I HATE jerky but LOVE Beest. It's salty, savory and meets all my macros as someone with insulin resistance. Skip the jerky and go Beest!'
findings.therefore: The campaign targets jerky skeptics, not jerky lovers - 'the jerky upgrade for people who hate jerky' is the positioning

findings.finding: 8% of 38 reviews mention gifting/sharing; complaints run 3% - small but real critical mass
findings.therefore: The Charcuterie Trail Mix gets an occasion play (parties, gifting) while complaints inform demo talking points

findings.finding: Audit (6 public sources): 2026 KeHE Golden Ticket winner with fast-track access to all 12 KeHE DCs - nationwide doors are opening NOW, before consumer awareness exists
findings.therefore: The campaign is a launch-window sprint: be the brand buyers discover when the doors open, not after

findings.finding: Patent-pending crunch process 'verified through acoustic lab testing' + Non-UPF Verified + BRCGS AA facility + 46-52g protein, 0g added sugar per bag
findings.therefore: 'Crunch, Verified' is ownable: a measurable, provable claim no jerky competitor can copy - the crunch is literally measurable

programs.name: Crunch-Test Demo Days
programs.mechanic: 8 weekend demo shifts at Austin-area fitness studios, farmers markets, and partner retail (Central Market/HEB where stocked); blind crunch-off: BEEST vs. the jerky shoppers actually buy, judged by sound and texture. QR to '$3 off 2 bags' code. Controls: same stores, coupon only.

programs.name: The Charcuterie Board in a Bag
programs.mechanic: Occasion program for the Charcuterie Trail Mix: pitch to Austin event venues, corporate offices, and KeHE buyers as the shelf-stable party/gifting answer - 'a charcuterie board without the board.' 200-unit 'Board Box' pilot for 10 local hosts + PR kit.

programs.name: I Hate Jerky
programs.mechanic: 3 Austin food/fitness creators who publicly dislike jerky try BEEST on camera - blind crunch test, macro reveal at the end. Tagline: 'I HATE jerky but LOVE Beest.' Link to store finder + code CRUNCH. #ad disclosure.

programs.name: Crunch, Verified Proof Kit
programs.mechanic: The proof engine: acoustic-lab crunch data, Non-UPF verification, and the founders' family-diabetes story packaged into a one-page sell sheet for KeHE buyers + retailers + press; 3 short founder videos ('we measured the crunch') + email/SMS to the existing list ending in the starter pack.

slides.title: Campaign Overview
bullets: Thesis: BEEST does not need more awards - it needs shoppers to hear the crunch once and never go back [O1].
Problem: the 2026 KeHE Golden Ticket opens nationwide doors NOW, but with 2 employees and DTC-only sales, nothing on shelf says 'this is not the jerky you hate' [S3][R5].
Opportunity: the crunch is literally measurable - patent-pending process, acoustic-lab verified, 0g added sugar, 46-52g protein [S1][R6].
Solution: 'Crunch, Verified' proves the difference in person - blind crunch tests, charcuterie occasions, and a proof kit for buyers [O1][R6].
45-day goal: 1,200 attributed purchases and sample-to-purchase tracked against control stores [O1].
slides.notes: Open with the timing: Golden Ticket doors are opening while nobody knows the brand. The crunch is the proof point.

slides.title: The Product
bullets: Crunchy Jerky Chips: beef (48g protein) and pork (46g protein) - 0g sugar, ~230 cal, crunch 'through and through' via patent-pending process [S1][S9].
Charcuterie Trail Mix: pork jerky chips + parmesan crisps + roasted almonds - 52g protein, 0g added sugar, 7g fiber; 'a charcuterie board in a bag' [S1].
Non-UPF Verified, BRCGS Grade AA facility, Made in USA; ~$10-13/bag online, multipacks for retail [S1].
Sold DTC, Amazon, Austin/California independents; nationwide via KeHE (Golden Ticket) + Faire wholesale [S1][S3].

visual.desc: Three product bags fanned with a crunch 'sound wave' graphic and macro callouts

slides.notes: The crunch is the differentiator - jerky is a chore to eat, these are chips. Show the texture.

slides.title: The Company & Its Position
bullets: Founded 2023 by Lucas Prado & Nicole Ruiz - industrial engineers, husband-and-wife; product began as a family recipe -> university thesis -> 8 years scaling in South America -> Austin [S2][S4].
2026 KeHE Trend Finder Golden Ticket Winner - fast-track to all 12 KeHE DCs; RangeMe Top 50; Forbes July 2026 [S1][S3].
Competitors: Jack Link's, Chomps, traditional jerky brands - none offer a verified-crunch chip format in the meat-snack set [S5].
Position: real-food protein snack for people who hate jerky's texture - crunch-verified, 0 sugar, macro-clean [S9][R2].

visual.desc: Left: recognition timeline (2023 founding -> 2026 Golden Ticket/Forbes/RangeMe). Right: positioning map (x = texture: tough jerky to crunchy chip, y = protein: standard to 50g+) with BEEST alone in the crunchy-high-protein quadrant

slides.notes: The credentials are real - Golden Ticket is one of the most competitive validations in natural foods. The gap is consumer awareness.

slides.title: Target Market
bullets: P1 Macro-Driven Snackers, 18-34: Austin/DFW/Texas gym-goers and students who count protein grams and have been burned by chalky protein snacks [S5][R2].
P2 Clean-Label Parents & Hosts, 30-55: weekly shoppers buying no-added-sugar snacks for families and planning party/game-day/gifting occasions [S6][R4].
Both share one need: a meat snack that doesn't feel like a compromise - the crunch IS the proof [R1][R6].
Market: meat snacks +11.3% to $6.4B; 'real food / non-UPF' is the fastest-rising consumer demand in the aisle [S5][S6].

slides.title: Research Method & Results
bullets: Secondary (complete): press room, LinkedIn, Forbes, KeHE/RangeMe announcements, category data - 8 sources [S1][S3][S4][S5].

Primary, no-survey so far (complete): keyword-coded analysis of 38 public Judge.me reviews [R1][R2][R4] + distribution audit of 6 sources [R5][R6] [S10]; survey/interviews/competitor audit scheduled in-window (M1-M3 pending).

Key results: taste/crunch dominate reviews; one verbatim says 'I HATE jerky but LOVE Beest' [R1][R2]; Golden Ticket doors opening before awareness exists [R5]; crunch is patent-pending and lab-verified [R6].
Influences: protein-snack boom (social), non-UPF/clean-label demand (cultural), meat-snack growth +11.3% (market), KeHE timing (technological/distribution) [S5][S6].

visual.desc: Review theme chart (taste 42%, texture 21%, vs-jerky 18%) + distribution timeline

slides.notes: Be honest: n=38 is small - say so. The verbatim 'I HATE jerky but LOVE Beest' quote is the hook. Primary methods run in-window.

slides.title: Insights -> Campaign Decisions
bullets: Finding: 'I HATE jerky but LOVE Beest' is a verbatim review; 18% compare it to jerky directly [R1][R2] -> target jerky skeptics, not jerky lovers.
Finding: Golden Ticket opens doors NOW with zero consumer awareness [R5] -> sprint the launch window, don't coast.
Finding: crunch is patent-pending + acoustic-lab verified [R6] -> make the crunch audible and measurable in every demo.
Finding: 8% mention gifting; trail mix IS a charcuterie board [R4][S1] -> add the occasion play for parties/gifting.
Finding: real complaints exist (avg 4.34, not 5.0) [R1] -> demo talking points address texture expectations honestly.
slides.notes: Every decision traces to a finding. The 'I hate jerky' quote is the emotional center.

slides.title: Campaign Strategy
bullets: Big idea: Crunch, Verified - the only jerky chip whose crunch is proven, not promised. Message: 'Hear that? That's the difference.'
Positioning: for snackers who want jerky's protein without jerky's chore - BEEST is the crunchy, 0-sugar, macro-clean upgrade [S9][R2].
IMC mix: Paid (geo social) + Earned (Golden Ticket/Forbes story) + Shared (#CruncHVerified duets) + Owned (email/SMS, shelf cards, B2B proof kit).
Push-pull: KeHE/retail buyers get a proof kit and velocity test (push); shoppers get crunch tests and a code (pull) [O1][O2].

visual.desc: Key visual: jerky chip mid-crunch with acoustic sound-wave rings, 'Crunch, Verified' lockup

slides.notes: Point to the positioning: 'jerky's protein without jerky's chore.' The acoustic verification is the ownable claim.

slides.title: Program 1: Crunch-Test Demo Days
bullets: Crunch, Verified in person: 8 weekend demo shifts at Austin fitness studios, farmers markets, and partner retail; control stores get the code only [O1][O2].
Mechanic: blind crunch-off - BEEST vs. the jerky shoppers actually buy; judged by sound and texture; QR to '$3 off 2 bags'; ~200 samples per shift = 1,600 total [A7][A8].
Why: the product converts jerky-haters on first bite - 'I HATE jerky but LOVE Beest' - and most shoppers have never heard of it [R1][R2][R5].
Measured: QR scans per venue and sample-to-purchase vs. control [O1].

slides.title: Program 2: The Charcuterie Board in a Bag
bullets: Crunch, Verified for occasions: pitch the Charcuterie Trail Mix to Austin venues, offices, and KeHE buyers as the shelf-stable party/gifting answer [O1][O3].
Board Box pilot: 10 local hosts get a trail-mix bag + insert card - real occasions generate real content and reviews [A12].
Why: 8% of reviews mention gifting and the product literally IS a charcuterie board - an occasion jerky never owned [R4][S1].
KeHE timing: Golden Ticket doors open through 2027 - the proof kit lands while buyers are deciding placement [A14].

bullets: Crunch, Verified online: 3 Austin creators who publicly dislike jerky try BEEST blind - crunch test, macro reveal at the end; 'I HATE jerky but LOVE Beest' is the caption hook [O1][O3].
Every video links to the store finder + code CRUNCH with #ad disclosure [A17].
Proof Kit: acoustic-lab crunch data + Non-UPF verification + the family-diabetes founder story in a one-page sell sheet for KeHE buyers and press [S1][S4].
Named credibility: Golden Ticket, RangeMe Top 50, Forbes July 2026 - the proof kit leads with these [S1][S3].

slides.title: Proposed Budget & Financial Viability
bullets: Total $9,000: media $3,000; creators $1,950; demos $1,800; Board Box $800; production $600; tools $250; contingency $600 [A4][A6][A7][A9][A10][A11][A12].
Funnel: 800K x 1.5% x 10% = 1,200 purchases at $22 = $26.4K [A1][A4].
The $3 code is manufacturer-funded, netted in revenue [A1][A8].
GP 45% = $11.9K; profit ROI 32%; ROAS 5.3x [A2].
Conservative (50%): ROI ~-34%; 25% repeat + KeHE openings recover it [A13][A14]. Upside: ~240 demo purchases [A15].

slides.title: Impact & Measurement
bullets: O1: attributed purchases; baseline 0; target 1,200; code reports + UTMs; weekly [O1].
O1: sample-to-purchase vs. control; baseline week-0 [A3]; target 12%; QR + code match; weekly [O1].
O2: samples and claims; baseline 0; target 1,600 and 4,000; tally + coupon platform; weekly [O2].
O3: 800K impressions; 'crunch verified' recall baseline = in-window intercept survey n=100, post-campaign survey; target +8 pts [O3].
Trigger: under 15 QR scans per shift by week 3, move demos to top 2 venues; creator CTR under 1%, shift spend to Meta [A4].

slides.title: Why It Matters
bullets: Thesis: BEEST does not need more awards - it needs shoppers to hear the crunch once and never go back. Crunch, Verified turns retail sampling into believers [O1].
Projected: 1,200 purchases and $11.9K gross profit on $9K (32% ROI), plus a sample-to-purchase readout BEEST takes to every KeHE buyer [A1][O1].
Mission: real food for real macros - a family recipe that took 8 years and a patent to make crunchy; every crunch-verified bag is a shopper who stopped settling for tough jerky [S4][R2].
Next: if sample-to-purchase beats 12%, scale Crunch-Test demos to KeHE launch markets as doors open [O1][A14].
